claim: UK occupational pension scheme trustees must invest scheme assets in the best interests of members and beneficiaries, and in their sole interest where there is a potential conflict of interest.
passage: in the best interests of members and beneficiaries; and ... in the case of a potential conflict of interest, in the sole interest of members and beneficiaries
notes: Regulation 4 does not apply to schemes with fewer than 100 members (regulation 7, not fetched). It is a duty on trustees, not on the asset manager.

claim: Before investing, trustees must obtain and consider proper advice on whether the investment is satisfactory, and must decide how often to take such advice on investments they keep.
passage: the trustees must obtain and consider proper advice on the question whether the investment is satisfactory
notes: This is why an investment consultant or other adviser normally sits between the manager and the trustee decision.

claim: Trustees may delegate investment discretion to a fund manager and are not responsible for the manager's acts or defaults only if they have taken all reasonable steps to satisfy themselves about the manager's knowledge, experience and competence.
passage: if they have taken all such steps as are reasonable to satisfy themselves ... that he is carrying out his work competently
notes: The statutory protection depends on continuing checks, so a trusted manager is still monitored.

claim: Trustees must run a qualifying competitive tender, with bids from at least three unconnected providers, when selecting fiduciary management providers for 20% or more of scheme assets; the duty has sat in pensions regulations overseen by The Pensions Regulator since 1 October 2022.
passage: carry out a qualifying tender process when selecting FMPs in relation to 20% or more of the scheme's assets ... bids from at least three unconnected FMPs
notes: Guidance page last updated August 2022; later amendments were not checked. The duty originated in the CMA's 2019 Order.

claim: The CMA found in 2018 that firms providing both investment consultancy and fiduciary management had an incumbency advantage, that half of schemes bought fiduciary management from their existing consultant, and that some trustees showed low engagement in choosing and monitoring providers.
passage: firms which provide both investment consultancy and fiduciary management have an incumbency advantage ... Half of pension schemes buy fiduciary management from their existing investment consultant
notes: A finding about the market at that time and about consultant-led fiduciary management. It does not describe any named asset manager, and the market has been regulated differently since 2019.

claim: For investments, the FCA Consumer Duty applies to business with customers who are not professional clients, but it also reaches firms that determine or materially influence retail customer outcomes anywhere in the distribution chain, even without a direct relationship.
passage: For investments, the Duty applies to business conducted with a customer who is not a professional client ... The Duty applies across the distribution chain
notes: Guidance published July 2022. How the Duty applies to any particular fund or firm depends on facts not examined here.

claim: FCA rule COBS 2.1.1R requires a firm to act honestly, fairly and professionally in accordance with the best interests of its client.
passage: COBS 2.1.1R, 'the client's best interests rule' (wording from search-result text; Handbook page not readable by the fetch tool)
notes: Exact current wording and the scope of application to professional clients were not read on the primary page.

claim: LCP counted 367 UK pension buy-ins totalling £38.2bn in 2025, after £49.1bn in 2023 and £47.8bn in 2024.
notes: One consultancy's count; other consultancies report slightly different transaction numbers. Volumes are insured liabilities, not assets lost by any particular manager.

claim: FCA Principle 7 requires a firm to pay due regard to the information needs of its clients and communicate information to them in a way which is clear, fair and not misleading; it continues to apply to customers outside the scope of the Consumer Duty.
passage: communicate information to them in a way which is clear, fair and not misleading (FG22/5 para 4.2; para 2.11 on continued application)
notes: Read as quoted in FCA guidance FG22/5, not on the Handbook page itself.
